messages:
ana: hey folks — onboarding a customer with on-prem GPU racks in ap-southeast. They asked for an egress allowlist and proxy guidance. What exact source ranges and ports should we give them? they run an outbound HTTP proxy + DNS SRV for service discovery, and they mentioned they preserve source ports in some zones — any SNAT/persistent-port gotchas?

infra-bot: deploy 8345 for apac-edge-01 completed on 2025-11-19 — nodes reporting READY, healthchecks passing.

mike: short answer: give them a small stable set of source CIDRs + ports to allow. details:
- Control plane callbacks and runtime telemetry: outbound TCP 443 to our API endpoints.
- Healthchecks and readiness probes from our LBs: TCP 8080 and 8443 (we run both plain and TLS probes depending on customer config).
- Metrics/telemetry (Prometheus remote-write / ingest): TCP 443 (TLS).
- Container image pulls / package updates (if customer allows node internet access): 80/443 to common registries (we usually recommend customers block this and let us push images).
- If customer uses an intercepting HTTP proxy (CONNECT-only), our runtime will use CONNECT for TLS. If the proxy rewrites SNI/does TLS inspect, some models' host-based routing can break.

Also: ephemeral SNAT port exhaustion is the biggest gotcha. On small NAT pools our goroutine-heavy telemetry + batching can exhaust ephemeral ports and result in 5xx for a subset of pods. Recommend they either: increase ephemeral port pool (>= 32k), or allocate a larger NAT pool, or allow our small set of static egress IPs so SNAT is avoided for these flows.

sean: adding specifics for the APAC edge we just provisioned — we can offer these stable CIDR blocks to customers that want to whitelabel: 
```
apac-edge-01: 203.0.113.96/27
apac-edge-02: 203.0.114.0/27
apac-egress-health: 198.51.100.16/28
management-proxy: 198.51.100.32/28
```
Note: these are anycasted from our edge POPs; customers should allow them as destination CIDRs in their outbound firewall (i.e., their firewalls must allow traffic TO these ranges from the cluster nodes). If the customer insists on hostname-only allowlisting (proxy only), we need to run healthchecks via proxy mode which implies CONNECT + preserved ports behavior.

julia: some customer-side guidance to pass along:
- Allow outbound TCP ports: 443, 8443, 8080, and ephemeral high ports for callbacks if they don't want static SNAT.
- If they have strict egress proxies: ensure the proxy allows the CONNECT verb to our hostnames and does NOT terminate TLS for our API endpoints (or provide a CA bundle and we can adapt).
- DNS / service discovery: because we use SRV records for internal failover, they should not hard-cache DNS for long TTLs — allow normal resolution. If they put a proxy that does DNS-over-HTTP and re-resolves to different egress IPs, that will break session affinity for LBs.

support-ops: can someone paste a copy-paste snippet for customers? helps them not screw up the ACL.

mike: sure — paste this JSON into their firewall ticket (replace with chosen region blocks):
```json
{
  "purpose": "Redwood inference egress for on-prem GPU nodes",
  "sources": ["<customer-node-cidr-blocks>"] ,
  "destinations": [
    {"cidr": "203.0.113.96/27", "ports": [443, 8443, 8080]},
    {"cidr": "203.0.114.0/27", "ports": [443]},
    {"cidr": "198.51.100.16/28", "ports": [443]},
    {"cidr": "198.51.100.32/28", "ports": [443]}
  ],
  "notes": "If customer uses an HTTP proxy, ensure CONNECT is allowed and TLS is not intercepted for api.redwood.example.com. If customer preserves source ports, confirm ephemeral port availability or allow the static CIDRs above to avoid SNAT issues."
}
```

sean: extra tech note — for customers behind Microsoft/Azure load balancers: some healthprobes come from variable source ports and probe IPs can change during internal maintenance. We recommend listing our CIDR blocks rather than LB source IPs in Azure. Also Azure NAT Gateway will preserve source port if configured, but basic SNAT from ILB won't.

ana: tagging @julia — do we have an RFC or KB we can link to for customers that want to avoid SNAT port exhaustion?

julia: yep — internal doc: https://intra.redwood/ops/egress-port-guidance (share with customer ops). main recs: increase ephemeral port range, use larger NAT pool, or accept our static egress CIDRs. Also mention monitoring: they should watch for RTOs and 4xx/5xx patterns that correlate with bursts.

ana: perfect. i'll send the JSON snippet + a short note about SNAT and the proxy CONNECT recommendation. thanks all :thumbsup:
